analyst.summary: Hindustan Zinc had a record FY26 (revenue up ~20%, profit up 34%) on the back of near four-year-high zinc prices and record silver prices, not on meaningfully higher volumes -- its own mined and refined output grew only mid-single digits, and its silver output actually fell 9% on declining ore grades. The company remains one of the world's lowest-cost zinc producers and has sharply strengthened its balance sheet (debt-to-equity down from 0.80x to 0.36x in a year), and is guiding a further, capex-funded volume recovery in FY27, including a rebound in silver output. Set against that: nearly all of the company's free cash flow is currently being paid out as dividend or ploughed into growth capex, leaving little buffer if zinc and silver prices retrace from today's elevated, largely supply-disruption-driven levels; and the stock carries a persistent governance overhang from the Vedanta parent's cash needs (a disputed related-party brand-fee payment had to be partly refunded after regulatory scrutiny) and a still-unresolved, periodically-selling Government of India stake. At roughly 16x trailing earnings and a ~4% dividend yield, the valuation is not extreme, but it does not offer much margin of safety against a commodity-price normalization either. We rate it a Hold: a genuinely well-run, low-cost franchise, but not one to add to at a point that looks closer to the top of its earnings cycle than the bottom.
